answer: That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Because the kernel cliff is fixed at deposit and entered in the terrace ledger, the cipher audit makes public how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 15 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That is 21 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
